subject: E0001: Partition distinct radix HT on group-key hash

audit.mechanism: For a grouped aggregate with DISTINCT aggregates, DuckDB first deduplicates (G, x) in a separate radix-partitioned hash table, then feeds the distinct rows into the main aggregate table on G. Before this change, the distinct table picked its partition from the hash of all of (G, x). Each distinct partition therefore held pieces of nearly every group, and re-aggregating a partition into the main table touched almost all groups. Now the radix-partition bits of the distinct table's hash come from the hash of G alone, and the rest of the hash (low bits used for HT slots, top 16 salt bits) still comes from the full (G, x) hash. As a result, each distinct partition holds whole groups, and its re-aggregation into the main table stays local. The prefix hash is built the same way as the main table's group hash (Hash of the first column, then CombineHash of the rest), so the partitions line up. This is standard co-partitioning on the outer grouping key.
audit.trigger: Set up in the PhysicalHashAggregate constructor: `if (estimated_cardinality >= DISTINCT_GROUP_PARTITION_THRESHOLD)` (src/execution/operator/aggregate/physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:192). Then, for each grouping set, `if (!grouping.HasDistinct() || grouping_sets[i].empty()) continue;` (:195), and each distinct radix table gets `radix_table->partition_prefix_count = grouping_sets[i].size();` (:200). At sink time: `if (prefix_count != 0 && prefix_count < group_chunk.ColumnCount() && group_chunk.size() != 0)` (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:574). Using the first k columns as G is valid because the distinct table's grouping_set is an ordered set: the group indices are inserted first (`grouping_set.insert(group)`, distinct_aggregate_data.cpp:97), and the distinct children come after them at `set_idx + group_by_size` (:101). In short, the path is taken for any hash aggregate with a non-empty GROUP BY (per grouping set) and at least one DISTINCT aggregate, when the optimizer's cardinality estimate for the aggregate is at least 4096. There are no type, schema or query-shape tests.
audit.constants: There are two constants. (1) `DISTINCT_GROUP_PARTITION_THRESHOLD = 4096` (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:191) is compared against the operator's estimated_cardinality. No reason is given for it. It is a round power of two, likely chosen to avoid the cost on tiny inputs, and is not obviously fitted to TPC-H sizes: q16's aggregate estimate is far above it at any scale factor. Just below 4096 the old path runs unchanged. The cost of being on the wrong side is small either way: the change only affects partition locality, plus the loss of the compressed/dictionary fast path (see fallback). The author also points out a possible skew issue when there are few groups but a large estimate, and there is no gate for it. (2) `RADIX_MASK = RadixPartitioning::Mask(RadixPartitioning::MAX_RADIX_BITS)` (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:592). MAX_RADIX_BITS = 12 is DuckDB's existing maximum ("4096 partitions ought to be enough", radix_partitioning.hpp:25-26), and Shift places it just below the 16-bit salt (:44-51). Splicing the full 12-bit window covers every radix-bit count the table may use when it repartitions. This is a structural constant, not a tuned one.
audit.natural_class: Any GROUP BY query with a DISTINCT aggregate whose estimate is at least 4096 rows, on any schema, with any key types, and including GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP (handled per set). Examples: `SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) FROM events GROUP BY user_id;` `SELECT country, device, COUNT(DISTINCT ip), SUM(DISTINCT amount) FROM web_logs GROUP BY ROLLUP(country, device);` The benefit is largest when there are many groups and each group has many distinct values.
audit.fallback: If the estimate is below 4096, the GROUP BY is empty, or there are no DISTINCT aggregates, partition_prefix_count stays 0 (default, radix_partitioned_hashtable.hpp) and `ht.AddChunk(group_chunk, payload_input, filter);` runs exactly as before (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:600). The only change on the old path is that `sink_count += groups.size()` moved: it is now incremented in the compressed-path return and in the pre-hashed overload (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:523, :565). The count is the same, so adaptivity behaviour is unchanged. On the new path, the distinct table calls the pre-hashed AddChunk overload directly, so it skips the TryAddCompressedGroups dictionary/constant fast path. That can be a small regression for distinct aggregates over dictionary-compressed inputs.
audit.label: general
audit.label_reason: I rate this "general". The technique is principled: partitioning the distinct pre-aggregation on the outer GROUP BY key, so each partition re-aggregates whole groups. It applies to every grouped DISTINCT aggregate, with no tests on schema, types or query shape. The only gate is one coarse cardinality floor (4096), whose origin is unexplained but which is not fitted to TPC-H's values. Two caveats keep it from being fully free: it gives up the dictionary-compressed sink fast path for distinct tables, and it has no protection against skew when there are few groups but a large estimate. Both are tuning concerns, not signs that it targets specific queries. The measured gain is only for q16, and the timings were noisy.
